purpose: interphase turns a request into an approved, testable spec and buildable Steps: it interviews the person until the intent is shared, writes the spec and its Steps, checks and reviews them, and hands them off with the repository unchanged.

objectives.text: Each run ends in a spec the person approved at the read-back and handed off with the repository unchanged.
Each spec states criteria whose tests prove them at named seams.
Each spec comes with Steps a builder can build, and rarely needs an amendment after hand-off.
The interview settles the intent in few rounds, with recommended answers the person mostly takes.
The guesses made after the interview each rest on a recorded intent line.
interphase's checks and its spec review find few errors in its drafts, and none remain at hand-off.
Each run's time and its own spend are known, by phase, by wait for the person and by model.

run.start.description: A run started: interphase took its guard snapshot of the repository before writing a spec or an amendment.
questions: Which runs amend a handed-off spec?

slug.description: The spec's slug, the name every file of the spec package starts with.
slug.measured_from: The docs/specs/<slug>.guard.json path named by the guard snapshot command.
slug.includes: The file name before its first dot.
slug.reading: Every run of one spec shares this value; a reused slug names a new spec's runs too.
slug.question: Which spec is this run about?

amends.description: The run id of the earlier run of this slug that this run amends.
amends.measured_from: The store at the moment of the snapshot: the slug's newest run in this repository, taken only when the record already said handed-off.
amends.includes: The run id of the slug's newest earlier run in this repository.
amends.excludes: Runs of other repositories and runs of a reused slug whose record was not handed off.
amends.reading: A run id means this run amends a handed-off spec; null means this run is not an amendment.
amends.question: Which run did this amendment correct?

amending.description: Whether this run amends a spec that was already handed off.
amending.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json at the moment of the snapshot: true when it exists with status handed-off.
amending.includes: Snapshots taken while the record says handed-off.
amending.excludes: Snapshots of a new spec, a reused slug whose record is absent or in progress included.
amending.reading: true means the run amends a handed-off spec; false means it writes a new spec.
amending.question: How often does a handed-off spec need an amendment?

round.recorded.description: The record check ran on the interview record without --complete, after interphase wrote a round, a seam, a criterion or a Step.
questions: How many record checks did the interview take?
How many errors did each record check find?

exit.description: The exit code of the record check as the shell reported it.
exit.measured_from: The hook payload of the Bash call: 0 when the call succeeded, the integer after "Exit code " on the first line of the error when it failed.
exit.includes: The exit code when the command runs exactly one of interphase's scripts and that script is the command's last part.
exit.excludes: Commands where anything runs after the script, such as an echo of its exit code, commands that run more than one of interphase's scripts, and interrupted commands.
exit.reading: 0 means the script passed; a higher number means it refused or failed. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
exit.question: Did the record check pass on this run of it?

errors.description: The number of lines the record check printed that start "error:".
errors.measured_from: A check's printed lines: the Bash call's stdout and stderr, or the error text after its first line when the call failed.
errors.includes: Every printed line starting "error:" when the command runs exactly one of interphase's scripts.
errors.excludes: Lines printed by any other part of the command, and every count on a command that runs more than one of interphase's scripts, whose outputs cannot be told apart.
errors.reading: Higher means the check found more errors in this draft; 0 means it found none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
errors.question: How many errors did the record check find at this point of the run?

warnings.description: The number of lines the record check printed that start "warning:".
warnings.measured_from: A check's printed lines: the Bash call's stdout and stderr, or the error text after its first line when the call failed.

warnings.excludes: Lines printed by any other part of the command, and every count on a command that runs more than one of interphase's scripts, whose outputs cannot be told apart.

review.done.description: The interphase:spec-reviewer agent returned its one review of the spec and its Steps.
questions: Did the review approve the spec?

approved.description: Whether the spec reviewer approved the spec.
approved.measured_from: The reviewer's reply: true when its first non-empty line is "Status: Approved", false when it is "Status: Issues found".
approved.excludes: Any judgement in the reply's prose.
approved.reading: true means approved; false means issues were found. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
approved.question: Did interphase's spec pass its review?

issues.description: The number of issues the spec reviewer raised.
issues.measured_from: The reviewer's reply: the lines after its Status line that start "- ".
issues.includes: Every issue line the reviewer wrote.
issues.excludes: Prose lines that do not start "- ".
issues.reading: Higher means the review found more issues; 0 means it found none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
issues.question: How many issues did the review find in the spec?

exit.measured_from: The hook payload of the Bash call: 0 when the call succeeded, the integer after "Exit code " on the first line of the error when it failed.
exit.includes: The exit code when the command runs exactly one of interphase's scripts and that script is the command's last part.
exit.excludes: Commands where anything runs after the script, such as an echo of its exit code, commands that run more than one of interphase's scripts, and interrupted commands.

clean.measured_from: The guard verify's exit code and its printed error lines: false when the exit code is a non-zero integer or an error line was printed.
clean.includes: The verify's own exit code and error lines.
clean.excludes: Changes inside the spec package, which the guard allows.
clean.reading: true means the tree matched the snapshot; false means it differed. Null means both the exit code and the error count are unknown.
clean.question: Did interphase change anything outside its spec package?

summary.description: One line per run, rebuilt after every event: what the run produced, how its interview, checks and review went, where its time went and what its own messages cost.

slug.measured_from: The summary builder's --slug argument, the slug of the run's events.
slug.includes: The file name before its first dot.
slug.reading: Every run of one spec shares this value.
slug.question: Which spec is this run about?

status.measured_from: The run's events: the last run.handoff's clean.
status.includes: handed-off when the last guard verify was clean, guard-difference when it found a difference, in-progress before any guard verify.
status.excludes: Anything after the run's last event.
status.reading: handed-off means the run ended with the repository unchanged; guard-difference means the verify found a change; in-progress means no hand-off yet. Null means the last verify's result is unknown.
status.question: Did the run reach hand-off?

pathway.description: The pathway that wrote the spec.
pathway.measured_from: The spec file docs/specs/<slug>.md: the name in its line "Pathway: <name>.".
pathway.reading: Names the kind of request. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
pathway.question: Which kinds of request does interphase run on?

lane.description: Whether the spec is a brief or a full spec.
lane.measured_from: The spec file docs/specs/<slug>.md: brief when it holds the line "Lane: brief.", full otherwise.
lane.reading: brief means a short spec without an interview; full means a full spec. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
lane.question: How many runs wrote a brief rather than a full spec?

attended.description: Whether a person answered the interview.
attended.measured_from: The decisions file docs/specs/<slug>.decisions.md: false when every "- I<n>" line of its Intent section ends "(inferred)".
attended.includes: The intent lines of the decisions file.
attended.reading: true means a person stated the intent; false means interphase inferred every intent line. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
attended.question: How many runs were interviewed and how many ran unattended?

amends.description: The run id of the earlier run this run amends.
amends.includes: The slug's newest earlier run in the repository when the record was already handed off.
amends.reading: A run id means this run is an amendment; null means it is not.
amends.question: How often does a handed-off spec need an amendment?

amendment.description: The amendment number this run wrote.
amendment.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json: the highest amendment among its Steps, taken only when the run amends an earlier one.
amendment.excludes: Runs that write a new spec.
amendment.reading: 1 or higher numbers the amendment; null means the run is not an amendment or its record is absent.
amendment.question: How many times has this spec been amended?

lead_seconds.measured_from: The run's events: the seconds from the first event's ts to the last's.
lead_seconds.includes: Everything between the guard snapshot and the run's latest event, waits for the person included.
lead_seconds.reading: Higher means the run took longer; 0 means it holds one event so far.
lead_seconds.question: How long does a run take from snapshot to hand-off?

wait_seconds.description: The time the run spent waiting for the person.
wait_seconds.measured_from: The session transcripts: for each message the person typed, or each read-back answer, inside the run's span, the seconds since the latest assistant message before it.
wait_seconds.includes: Typed messages and answers to AskUserQuestion inside the run's span.
wait_seconds.excludes: Every other tool result and the subagents' transcripts.
wait_seconds.reading: Higher means more of the lead time was spent waiting for the person; 0 means none. Null means no main transcript of the run's sessions was found.
wait_seconds.question: How much of a run's time is the person's?

phases.description: The time spent in each phase of the run, in time order.
phases.measured_from: The run's events: the spans between the landmarks run.start, the first round.recorded, the first steps.checked, the last readback.asked, the first spec.rendered, the last check or review after that render, and run.handoff.
phases.includes: Each span between two landmarks present in time order.
phases.excludes: Landmarks that are absent or earlier than the landmark kept before them.
phases.reading: Each entry names the phase a span ends; a missing phase means its landmark did not occur. Null means the run's events were absent.
phases.question: Where does a run's time go?

items.measured_from: Two consecutive landmark events of the run.
items.reading: Each entry is one span of the run.
items.question: How long did this phase take?

phase.description: The phase's name: ground for the first span, otherwise named for the landmark that ends it.
phase.measured_from: The landmark that ends the span: interview for steps.checked, read-back for readback.asked, write for spec.rendered, review for the last check or review, hand-off for run.handoff.
phase.reading: Names the phase the seconds belong to.
phase.question: Which phase is this?

seconds.measured_from: The seconds between the two landmarks' ts.
seconds.reading: Higher means the phase took longer; 0 means both landmarks fell in the same second.
seconds.question: How long did this phase take?

sessions.description: The number of Claude Code sessions the run spanned.
sessions.measured_from: The run's events: the distinct non-null session values.
sessions.includes: Every session that wrote one of the run's events.
sessions.reading: 1 means the run stayed in one session; higher means it was resumed in others. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
sessions.question: How often does a run span several sessions?

intent_lines.measured_from: The decisions file docs/specs/<slug>.decisions.md: the "- I<n>" lines.
intent_lines.reading: Higher means the intent was stated in more lines. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
intent_lines.question: How much intent did the interview settle?

rounds.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json: the length of its rounds list.
rounds.includes: The intent round and every frontier round.
rounds.reading: Higher means the interview took more rounds; null with a record present means it holds no rounds list. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
rounds.question: How many rounds does an interview take?

questions.description: The number of questions the interview asked.
questions.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json: the sum of its rounds entries' questions.
questions.reading: Higher means the interview asked more questions. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
questions.question: How many questions does an interview ask?

recommended.description: The number of answers the person took as recommended.
recommended.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json: the questions minus the changed answers over its rounds entries.
recommended.includes: Every answer that matched interphase's recommended answer.
recommended.reading: Higher means more of interphase's recommendations were taken as they stood. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
recommended.question: How much of the interview did interphase get right on its own?

changed.description: The number of answers the person changed from the recommended one.
changed.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json: the sum of its rounds entries' changed.
changed.includes: Every answer that differed from the recommendation.
changed.reading: Higher means the person changed more recommendations; 0 means every recommendation was taken. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
changed.question: How often does the person correct interphase's recommendations?

readbacks.description: The number of questions answered through AskUserQuestion during the run, such as the read-back.
readbacks.measured_from: The run's events: the readback.asked events.
readbacks.includes: Every AskUserQuestion answer in the run's sessions while the run was open.
readbacks.reading: Higher means more read-backs before the spec was written; 0 means none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
readbacks.question: How many read-backs did the run need?

approved.description: Whether the person's read-back led to the spec being written.
approved.measured_from: The run's events: true when a spec.rendered follows the last readback.asked, false when read-backs were asked and no render follows.
approved.includes: The read-backs and renders of the run.
approved.reading: true means the spec was written after the last read-back; false means it was not written yet. Null means no read-back was asked.
approved.question: Did the read-back reach an approved spec?

decisions.measured_from: The decisions file docs/specs/<slug>.decisions.md: the "- " lines of its Decisions section.
decisions.reading: Higher means more decisions were recorded. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.

seams.question: How many seams does a spec test at?

criteria.question: How large is the spec?

unproven.reading: Higher means more criteria rest on proof the builder cannot run; 0 means none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
unproven.question: How much of the spec can the build prove?

varying.description: The number of criteria for behaviour that varies from run to run.
varying.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json: the criteria with varies.

msps.question: How many separate parts does a spec ship as?

steps_with_assumptions.description: The number of Steps that carry assumptions.
steps_with_assumptions.measured_from: The record file docs/specs/<slug>.record.json: the Steps with a non-empty assumptions list.
steps_with_assumptions.includes: Every Step with at least one assumption.
steps_with_assumptions.reading: Higher means more Steps rest on a guess made after the interview; 0 means none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
steps_with_assumptions.question: How many Steps rest on assumptions?

assumptions.description: The number of assumptions the spec lists.
assumptions.measured_from: The spec file docs/specs/<slug>.md: the "- " lines of its Assumptions subsection other than "- None".
assumptions.reading: Higher means interphase filled more gaps after the interview; 0 means it filled none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
assumptions.question: How many guesses did interphase make after the interview?

assumptions_by_intent.description: The number of assumptions citing each intent line, ordered by intent number.
assumptions_by_intent.measured_from: The spec file docs/specs/<slug>.md: each I<n> inside a "(relies on" parenthesis of its Assumptions lines.
assumptions_by_intent.includes: Every intent line cited, counted once per assumption line.
assumptions_by_intent.reading: An entry with a higher count means more guesses rest on that intent line; an empty list means no assumption cites one. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
assumptions_by_intent.question: Which intent lines do interphase's guesses rest on?

items.description: One intent line and the assumptions citing it.
items.reading: Each entry is one cited intent line.
items.question: How many guesses rest on this intent line?

intent.description: The intent line's id, such as I1.
intent.question: Which intent line is this?

count.description: The number of assumption lines citing this intent line.
count.includes: Each line once, however often it names the id.
count.excludes: Lines that do not cite it.
count.reading: Higher means more guesses rest on this intent line.
count.question: How many guesses rest on this intent line?

checks.description: Each of interphase's checks that ran during the run, with its errors on the first and last run.
checks.measured_from: The run's events round.recorded, steps.checked, spec.checked and items.checked.
checks.includes: Each check that ran at least once, in the order record, steps, spec, items.
checks.reading: Each entry describes one check; a check missing from the list never ran. Null means the run's events were absent.
checks.question: How many errors do interphase's first drafts carry, and how many remain?

items.measured_from: The run's events of that check.
items.question: How did this check go over the run?

check.description: The check: record for the record check, steps for the complete record check, spec for the spec check, items for the items check.
check.excludes: The guard verify and the review.
check.question: Which check is this?

runs.description: The number of times the check ran.
runs.measured_from: The run's events of that check.
runs.reading: Higher means the check ran more often; 1 means it ran once.
runs.question: How many attempts did the check take?

first_errors.description: The errors the check found the first time it ran.
first_errors.measured_from: The first event of that check: its errors.
first_errors.includes: Error lines of the first run.
first_errors.reading: Higher means the first draft carried more errors; 0 means none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
first_errors.question: How many errors did the first draft carry?

first_warnings.description: The warnings the check found the first time it ran.
first_warnings.measured_from: The first event of that check: its warnings.
first_warnings.includes: Warning lines of the first run.
first_warnings.reading: Higher means the first draft drew more warnings; 0 means none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
first_warnings.question: How many warnings did the first draft draw?

last_errors.description: The errors the check found the last time it ran.
last_errors.measured_from: The last event of that check: its errors.
last_errors.includes: Error lines of the last run.
last_errors.reading: 0 means the last draft passed the check; higher means errors remained. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
last_errors.question: Did the last draft pass the check?

review_approved.description: Whether the spec reviewer approved the spec.
review_approved.measured_from: The run's last review.done event: its approved.
review_approved.includes: The last review of the run.
review_approved.reading: true means approved; false means issues were found. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
review_approved.question: Did the spec pass its review?

review_issues.description: The number of issues the spec reviewer raised.
review_issues.measured_from: The run's last review.done event: its issues.
review_issues.includes: Issue lines of the last review.
review_issues.reading: Higher means the review found more issues; 0 means none. Null means the value is unknown or its source was absent; null is never zero.
review_issues.question: How many issues did the review find?

usd.description: What the run's own messages cost.
usd.measured_from: The session transcripts: each counted message's tokens of each kind times the price table's per-million price for its model and kind, divided by one million and rounded to 6 decimal places.
usd.includes: Only the run's own main-session messages and its own interphase:scout and interphase:spec-reviewer agents' messages timed from the run's first event to its last, both included, each message once by its id.
usd.excludes: The messages before the guard snapshot, which belong to the run of whatever started this one, records of the model <synthetic>, every other agent type, and every other plugin's spend.
usd.reading: Higher means the run cost more; 0 means it used no priced tokens. Null means a counted model has no price in the table, or the source was absent.
usd.question: What does an interphase run cost?

prices_date.description: The date of the price table the cost was computed with.
prices_date.measured_from: The date key of interphase's price table scripts/metrics_prices.json.
prices_date.reading: Names the date the prices were taken; a later table may price the same tokens differently.
prices_date.question: Which prices does usd use?

queries.name: runs_overview
queries.question: Which interphase runs happened in the last 30 days, newest first, with their status, pathway, lane, lead time and cost?
queries.sql: SELECT run, slug, status, pathway, lane, lead_seconds, usd, ts FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'interphase' AND CAST(ts AS TIMESTAMPTZ) >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY ORDER BY ts DESC

queries.name: phase_time
queries.question: How much time do interphase runs spend in each phase?
queries.sql: SELECT phase, sum(seconds) AS seconds, count(DISTINCT run) AS runs FROM (SELECT run, unnest(phases, recursive := true) FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'interphase') GROUP BY phase ORDER BY seconds DESC

queries.name: interview
queries.question: For each interviewed run, how many rounds and questions did the interview take and how many recommended answers did the person change?
queries.sql: SELECT run, rounds, questions, recommended, changed, readbacks, approved FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'interphase' AND rounds IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ts DESC

queries.name: assumptions_by_intent
queries.question: Which intent lines do the assumptions made after the interview rest on, and how often?
queries.sql: SELECT intent, sum("count") AS "count" FROM (SELECT unnest(assumptions_by_intent, recursive := true) FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'interphase') GROUP BY intent ORDER BY "count" DESC, intent

queries.name: checks_and_review
queries.question: For each run and check, how many times did the check run, with how many errors on its first and last run, and what did the spec review find?
queries.sql: SELECT run, review_approved, review_issues, "check", runs, first_errors, last_errors FROM (SELECT run, ts, review_approved, review_issues, unnest(checks, recursive := true) FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'interphase') ORDER BY ts DESC, run, "check"

queries.name: spend_by_model
queries.question: What did interphase's own runs spend on each model?
queries.sql: SELECT model, sum(usd) AS usd, sum(messages) AS messages FROM (SELECT unnest(models, recursive := true) FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'interphase') GROUP BY model ORDER BY usd DESC NULLS LAST, model

queries.name: amendments
queries.question: How often was each spec amended after hand-off?
queries.sql: SELECT slug, count(amends) AS amendments, count(*) AS runs FROM summaries WHERE plugin = 'interphase' GROUP BY slug ORDER BY amendments DESC, slug
